title: Chat requests (accept-first messaging for non-contacts)
status: SHIPPED backend on the Convex deployment. Native builds its own UI against the functions below.
concept: When a user taps Chat / Call / Video on someone who is NOT a contact, do NOT open the conversation directly. Instead send a chat request; the recipient accepts (which opens/creates the 1:1) or declines. Contacts keep opening the chat directly with no request.

opensDirectlyWhenAnyTrue: existingConversation — a 1:1 already exists between the two users
phoneSavedOnDevice — the SAME signal groupMemberProfile.getMemberProfile returns (a matched synced device contact). Enforced server-side.
acceptedContact — a contacts row (mine -> them) with status 'accepted' (same source as contacts.getContacts)
contactDefinition.note: The backend evaluates this itself on every send/accept, so the gate can never be bypassed by a stale client. The client should still call getChatEligibility first to decide whether to open the chat or show the request UI.

flow: 1. On tapping Chat/Call/Video, call chatRequests.getChatEligibility({ otherUserId }).
2. If requiresChatRequest is false → open the chat directly (use conversations.getOrCreateDirect as before).
3. If requiresChatRequest is true → show the request composer and call chatRequests.send({ toUserId, message? }).
4. Recipient sees pending requests via chatRequests.listIncoming and accepts (chatRequests.accept) or declines (chatRequests.decline).
5. On accept, the 1:1 conversation is created/opened and its id is returned.

returns.outgoingStatus: 'none' | 'pending' | 'accepted' | 'declined' — status of a request I sent them
returns.incomingStatus: 'none' | 'pending' | 'accepted' | 'declined' — status of a request they sent me

getChatEligibility.notes: Reactive. Returns all-false/none defaults when unauthenticated.

returns.conversationId: Id<conversations> | null — set when status is 'accepted' or 'already_contact'

behavior: already_contact: the two are actually contacts → no request created; conversationId is the (opened) 1:1. Just navigate there.
accepted: the other user had ALREADY sent me a pending request → mutual intent auto-accepts and opens the conversation.
pending: a new (or re-sent) request is now pending. Idempotent — re-sending updates the existing row rather than duplicating.
A previously declined outgoing request can be re-sent (goes back to pending).
errors: BAD_REQUEST — sending to yourself, or message too long
FORBIDDEN — either user has blocked the other
FORBIDDEN — caller is not the recipient, or a block exists
accept.notes: Idempotent: accepting an already-accepted request returns the same conversationId.

decline.notes: Recipient only. Row is kept as 'declined' so repeat sends don't spam.
errors: FORBIDDEN — caller is not the recipient

cancel.notes: Sender only. Deletes the outgoing request row.
errors: FORBIDDEN — caller is not the sender

listIncoming.returns: Array<RequestView> — pending requests addressed to me, newest first.

listOutgoing.returns: Array<RequestView> — requests I've sent, any status, newest first.

incomingCount.returns: number — count of pending incoming requests (for a badge).

RequestView.otherUserName: string — resolved to the name the viewer knows them by

notes: conversations.getOrCreateDirect is unchanged and still works for contacts (cases 1-3). The request gate is only for genuine strangers.
The same accept-first gate applies to Chat, Call, and Video: for a non-contact, send a chat request first; a call/video should only be offered once the conversation exists (i.e. after acceptance).
